title_en: Commentary on al-Jazariyyah — the last tape
body_ar:
سأعيد متن الباب السابق لتصحيح الأخطاء التي فيه، قال المؤلف رحمه الله:

واعْرِفْ لمقطوع وموصول وتا** في مصحف الإمام فيما قد أتى فاقطــــع بعــشر كلــــــــمات ألا** مـــعْ مَلْـــجَإٍ ولا إلـــــــــه إلا وتعبدوا يَاسِينَ ثاني هــــــودَ لا** يشركن تشركْ يدخُلَنْ تعلوا على ألَّا يقولوا لا أقولَ إمــــــــــــــا** بالرعد والمفتوح صل وعما نهوا اقطعوا مما بروم والنـسا** خلف المنافقــــين أمَّن أسسا فصلت النسا وذبــــــح حيثـما** وأن لم المفتوح كسر إنما الانعام والمفتوح يدعون مـعا** وخلف الانفال ونحل وقعا وكل ما سألتموه واخـــــتلف** ردوا كذا قل بيسما والوصل صف خلفتموني واشتروا في ما اقطعا** أوحي أفضتم اشتهت يبلو معا
body_en:
I shall repeat the text of the previous chapter in order to correct the errors in it. The author, may God have mercy on him, said:

*And know, for what is written separated and what is written joined, and for the tāʾ, in the codex of the Imam, in what has come down: separate in ten words — ألا with ملجإ, and لا إله إلا, and أن تعبدوا, [in] Yāsīn, the second [instance in] Hūd, لا يشركن, تشرك, يدخلن, تعلوا على, أن لا يقولوا, لا أقول, إما in al-Raʿd; and the one with the fatḥah, join; and عما نهوا, separate; مما in al-Rūm and al-Nisāʾ, with a difference of opinion in al-Munāfiqūn; أمن أسسا; فصلت al-Nisāʾ, and ذبح wherever it occurs; and أن لم with the fatḥah, break; إنما al-Anʿām, and the one with the fatḥah, يدعون, both; and a difference of opinion in al-Anfāl, and in al-Naḥl it occurred; and كل ما سألتموه, and they differed over ردوا; likewise قل بئسما, and as for the joined, describe [it]; خلفتموني and اشتروا in ما, separate; أوحي, أفضتم, اشتهت, يبلو, both.*

flags.context: the record consists almost entirely of verse listing which Qur'anic words are written joined and which separated in the Uthmanic codex
options: publish the English as a scaffold with the Arabic lemmata kept in Arabic, as here
publish the Arabic alone with an English note explaining what the chapter does
withhold the record from the English edition
flags.note: CRITICAL FOR DISPLAY, and a case the style guide does not squarely cover. This chapter is a mnemonic whose content is a list of individual Arabic words and the places in the Qur'an where each is written joined or separated. The list cannot be carried into English: translating the words destroys the point, since the point is how they are spelt, and the imperatives ('separate', 'join', 'break', 'describe') are instructions to a copyist that mean nothing without the Arabic. The rendering offered keeps every lemma in Arabic and translates only the frame; it is a scaffold for a reader following the Arabic, not a readable English text, and it should not be displayed as though it were one. Option 1 is recommended: present the Arabic with a prose note in English. A reviewer with expertise in rasm should check the rendering before either option is adopted.

flags.context: one of the lemmata in the list
flags.note: The word intended is بئسما of Sūrat al-Baqarah 2:93 and al-Aʿrāf 7:150. The source prints it without the hamzah, which is either an orthographic looseness of the transcription or a representation of the rasm being discussed — and in a chapter that is specifically about orthography that distinction matters. body_ar preserves the printed form; body_en gives the standard form so that the reader can identify the word. Flagged because in this chapter, unlike anywhere else in this range, an orthographic variant may be the subject rather than an error.

flags.arabic: سأعيد متن الباب السابق لتصحيح الأخطاء التي فيه
options: I shall repeat the text of the previous chapter in order to correct the errors in it
I shall repeat the matn of the previous chapter to correct the mistakes in it
I shall go over the previous chapter again to put right what was wrong
flags.note: Two points for the reviewer. First, the errors being corrected are errors in the recitation of the matn during the previous session, not errors in Ibn al-Jazari's text. Second, and more important for display: this sentence tells us that the published text is itself a correction of an earlier delivery, so the words that follow supersede something. What they supersede is not on this page, and may be on another page in the series.

translator_notes: Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.
The date shown by the CMS is a bulk-upload timestamp shared by every item in this range, not the date the Sheikh gave the answer. The real date of composition is unknown. See date_is_cms_bulk_upload.

This record belongs to the Sheikh's commentary on the Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah, Ibn al-Jazari's versified primer on the rules of Qur'anic recitation. The CMS holds the tapes out of order across ids 641–646 and the part numbers in the titles do not run with the ids; the series should be ordered by the number in the title, not by id.

EXCERPT ONLY. The published text breaks off and the full material is offered as a .docx download ('taḥmīl al-māddah'). The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends. The download-link label has been removed from body_ar as a navigation element and recorded in source_download_link.
'The codex of the Imam' renders muṣḥaf al-imām, the ʿUthmanic codex from which the standard written form (rasm) of the Qur'an derives.

The doubled asterisks in the source are the hemistich separators of the verse and are not part of the text. The elongated letters (kashīdah) in the source are typographic stretching used to justify the verse lines and carry no meaning; body_ar preserves them as served.

Per the style guide, verse is rendered as prose in italics with the Arabic kept in the bilingual pane and no rhymed English attempted. The unusual feature here is that the prose cannot carry the content either — see the first flag.
'A difference of opinion' renders khulf, the technical term for a divergence between the transmitters as to how a given word is written.
Sura names are given in transliteration rather than translated, since they function here as locations in the text.
